title: Drop core's stale cargo-deny exception for paste, which is no longer a dependency
goal: Vision: V-9. CEO direction 2026-11-16: apply the deny.toml fix in core. cargo deny check warns that core's exception for RUSTSEC-2024-0436 (paste) matches no crate: paste left Cargo.lock. A dead exception would silently hide the advisory if paste came back. Remove it, keep cargo deny check passing with no advisory warning.

reuse.searched: deny.toml and its readers in core: xtask/src/advisory_evidence.rs (config_with_database inserts db-path after the [advisories] line and keeps the rest byte for byte; its own tests use ignore=[]), xtask/src/distill/functional.rs and the release gates. A one-line policy change; nothing built.

limitations: Claimed --unscoped by CEO direction: deny.toml is reserved by the close receipt of T-CODEXSTEP120261101-5 (CODEXSTEP120261101, closed 2026-11-01), which comes from a line of history with a different root commit from today's main, so it can never settle by ancestry. Its deny.toml is an older version that this one-line change cannot collide with. The owner was asked on the board (item 1758) and told of this change.
cargo deny check was run on Linux x86_64 with cargo-deny 0.20.2; the policy also covers the Windows targets' graph, which was not run on Windows.
Main is unqualified development, not a release.
